question.prompt: Amy, Beth, and Jo listen to four different songs and discuss which ones they like. No song is liked by all three. Furthermore, for each of the three pairs of the girls, there is at least one song liked by those two girls but disliked by the third. In how many different ways is this possible?

solutions.explanation:
Describe each song by the set of girls who like it. Since all three cannot like a song, its liking set is either empty, a single girl, or one of the three pairs. Each pair must occur as a liking set at least once, so at least three of the four songs are liked by exactly two girls.

If exactly three songs are liked by pairs, the three pair types must each occur once. Choose the remaining song in \(4\) ways. It can be liked by nobody or by exactly one of the three girls, giving \(4\) possibilities. Assign the three pair types to the other three distinct songs in \(3\cdot2\cdot1=6\) ways. This case contributes
\[
4\cdot4\cdot6=96.
\]
If all four songs are liked by pairs, one pair type occurs twice and each other pair type occurs once. Choose the repeated type in \(3\) ways, its two songs in \(\binom42=6\) ways, and assign the remaining two types in \(2\) ways. This contributes
\[
3\cdot6\cdot2=36.
\]
These cases exhaust the possibilities and do not overlap. Within each case, the exceptional song or repeated pair type is uniquely determined, so no configuration is counted twice. The total is
\[
96+36=\boxed{132},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
solutions.title: Count three or four songs liked by pairs

solutions.explanation:
For each song, there are seven allowed liking sets: nobody, one of the three individual girls, or one of the three pairs. Thus \(7^4\) assignments satisfy the prohibition on all three girls liking a song.

We must keep only assignments in which all three pair types occur. If a specified pair type is missing, each song has \(6\) choices, giving \(6^4\) assignments. There are three possible missing pair types, so first subtract \(3\cdot6^4\).

An assignment missing two specified pair types was subtracted twice. Add back the \(5^4\) assignments for each of the three choices of two missing types. Finally, assignments missing all three pair types were initially counted once, subtracted three times, and added back three times. Subtract their \(4^4\) possibilities once more.

Consequently, an assignment with any missing pair type has net count zero, while an assignment with no missing type has count one. The required total is
\[
\begin{aligned}
7^4-3\cdot6^4+3\cdot5^4-4^4
&=2401-3888+1875-256\\
&=\boxed{132}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
